xpil_smooth_more — 2D smoothing op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "xpil_smooth_more", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Pillow's smoothing filter (strong version). Blurs more strongly than SMOOTH using the fixed kernel of PIL.ImageFilter.SMOOTH_MORE.

a, b are unused (fixed kernel).

The kernel is a 5x5 weighted mean (centre 44, its 8 neighbours 5, the outermost 16 pixels 1, divided by the total of 100). Because the centre weight is large, the blur is weaker than a uniform mean of the same 5x5; an impulse spreads only to about 44% at the centre + 5% each to the 8 adjacent pixels (measured: an impulse of 255 → centre 112, adjacent 13, outer ring 0). It acts more broadly than the 3x3 SMOOTH (centre 5, neighbours 1, total 13).

The input is clipped to [0,1] and turned into an 8-bit L image by truncating *255, and the output is converted back with /255 (introducing a 1/255 quantization). Pillow does not filter the outermost 2 pixels of the image, which keep their input values. A 0-size image is rejected with a ValueError and falls back fail-soft to the clipped input (recorded in the ledger). If you want a variable amount of blur, use gaussian or median. For removing noise before edge detection (xpil_contour /xpil_find_edges) or threshold.
